blocks.text: like, love, hate: -ing yoki to — nozik farq

Qizil kitobda **like / love / hate** dan keyin to ham, -ing ham kelishi va ma'no deyarli bir xilligini o'rgandik (→ qizil kitob, 52-dars). Ko'p hollarda bu to'g'ri: I **love cooking** = I **love to cook**. Lekin Britaniya ingliz tilida **like** bilan ko'pincha nozik farq seziladi. **like doing** — harakatning o'zidan zavq olish: I **like cooking** — «Ovqat pishirish menga yoqadi». **like to do** — biror ishni **to'g'ri, foydali** deb bilish va uni odat qilish; zavq shart emas: I **like to clean** the oven once a month — «Pechni oyiga bir marta tozalab turishni to'g'ri deb bilaman» (yoqmaydi, lekin kerak). O'zbekchada: «-ish menga yoqadi» va «-ishni odat qilganman / ma'qul ko'raman».

items.text: I **like cooking** for my friends — it relaxes me after work.
items.translation: Do'stlarimga **ovqat pishirish menga yoqadi** — ishdan keyin meni tinchlantiradi.

items.text: I **like to clean** the oven once a month, although I hate doing it.
items.translation: Pechni oyiga bir marta **tozalab turishni to'g'ri deb bilaman**, garchi buni yomon ko'rsam ham.

items.text: She **likes to arrive** early for interviews, just to be safe.
items.translation: U ish suhbatlariga har ehtimolga qarshi **erta borishni ma'qul ko'radi**.

blocks.text: **hate to** ko'pincha kechirim so'rash uchun ishlatiladi — gapiruvchi hozir qilmoqchi bo'lgan noxush ish haqida: I **hate to interrupt**, but ... — «Gapingizni bo'lganim uchun uzr, lekin ...»; I **hate to say** this, but ... — «Aytishga tilim bormaydi-yu, lekin ...». Bunday iboralarda -ing ishlatilmaydi.
would like / would love / would hate / would prefer + to

**would** qo'shilsa, ma'no o'zgaradi va deyarli doim **to** keladi: I**'d like to** go, I**'d love to** come, I**'d hate to** lose it, I**'d prefer to** wait. **like doing** — umuman, doimiy did: Do you **like dancing**? — «Raqs tushishni yaxshi ko'rasizmi?». **would like to do** — aniq bir vaziyatdagi istak yoki taklif: **Would** you **like to dance**? — «Raqsga tushasizmi?» (hozir). O'zbekchada: «yaxshi ko'raman» va «-moqchiman / istardim». Istisno — **would mind**: u -ing bilan qoladi: **Would** you **mind waiting**? Javobda to'liq fe'lni takrorlash shart emas: I'd **love to**! — «Jon deb!».

rows: I**'d love to travel** to Japan.
I**'d hate to fly** in this weather.

items.text: Do you **like playing** chess? — Yes, I play every weekend with my uncle.
items.translation: **Shaxmat o'ynashni yaxshi ko'rasizmi**? — Ha, har dam olish kuni amakim bilan o'ynayman.

items.text: Would you **like to play** a game of chess now? — Sure, why not?
items.translation: Hozir bir partiya **shaxmat o'ynaysizmi**? — Albatta, nega endi yo'q?

items.text: I'd **hate to lose** my job at the moment — prices are so high.
items.translation: Hozir **ishimni yo'qotishni sira istamasdim** — narxlar juda baland.

blocks.text: would like to have done: amalga oshmagan istak

O'tmishda bo'lmay qolgan istak haqida gapirish uchun ikkita teng shakl bor: **would like to have done** yoki **would have liked to do**: I**'d like to have seen** the film = I **would have liked to see** the film — «Filmni ko'rishni istagan edim (lekin ko'rmadim)». **would love / hate / prefer** bilan ham xuddi shunday: She**'d love to have been** there — «U yerda bo'lishni juda istagan edi». O'zbekchada «-ishni istagan edim, lekin ...», «-sam yaxshi bo'lardi» to'g'ri keladi. Ma'nosi **I wish I had ...** ga yaqin (→ 40-dars).

items.text: I'd **like to have gone** to the concert, but I had to work.
items.translation: Konsertga **borishni istagan edim**, lekin ishlashim kerak edi.

items.text: We **would have liked to see** more of Bukhara, but we only had one day.
items.translation: Buxoroni ko'proq **ko'rishni istagan edik**, lekin bor-yo'g'i bir kunimiz bor edi.

items.text: She'd **love to have been** there when her son scored the winning goal.
items.translation: O'g'li hal qiluvchi golni urganda u yerda **bo'lishni juda istagan edi**.

blocks.text: O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «I would like going to the cinema tonight.» → I**'d like to go** to the cinema tonight.; «Do you like to come with us?» (taklif) → **Would** you **like to come** with us?; «I like to travel» ni «Sayohat qilmoqchiman» deb tushunish — I like travelling / to travel — umuman yaxshi ko'raman, «-moqchiman» — I**'d like to** travel.; «I enjoy to dance.» → I **enjoy dancing**.; «I can't stand to wait.» → I **can't stand waiting**.; «I would like to see the film, but I missed it.» → I**'d like to have seen** it / I **would have liked to see** it.

Tekshirish usuli: o'zbekcha gapda «-moqchiman», «istardim», «-asizmi?» (taklif) bo'lsa — **would like to**. «Yaxshi ko'raman», «yoqadi» — **like -ing**. «Odat qilganman», «to'g'ri deb bilaman» — **like to do**. «Istagan edim, lekin bo'lmadi» — **would like to have done**.

rows: I **like to pay** bills on time.
would like / love / hate / prefer + to
I**'d like to have met** her.

examples.title: **love**, **hate**, **can't stand** + -ing: feelings
examples.description: Harakatga bo'lgan his-tuyg'u: yaxshi ko'rish, yomon ko'rish, toqat qila olmaslik. Bu ma'noda -ing eng tabiiy shakl.

sentences.text: Oliver **loves cycling** along the river on Sunday mornings.
sentences.translation: Oliver yakshanba tonglari daryo bo'ylab **velosiped haydashni juda yaxshi ko'radi**.

sentences.text: I **hate standing** in queues, so I do all my banking online.
sentences.translation: **Navbatda turishni yomon ko'raman**, shuning uchun bank ishlarimning hammasini onlayn qilaman.

sentences.text: Does your daughter **like going** to her new school? — Yes, she's made lots of friends.
sentences.translation: Qizingizga yangi maktabiga **borish yoqyaptimi**? — Ha, ko'p do'st orttirdi.

sentences.text: Most teenagers **dislike being** told what to do.
sentences.translation: Ko'pchilik o'smirlar nima qilish kerakligini **aytishlarini yoqtirmaydi**.

sentences.text: Nilufar **can't stand watching** horror films — she has nightmares for days.
sentences.translation: Nilufar qo'rqinchli film **ko'rishga toqat qila olmaydi** — keyin bir necha kun yomon tush ko'radi.

sentences.text: My grandfather **loves sitting** in the garden and chatting to the neighbours.
sentences.translation: Bobom bog'da **o'tirib**, qo'shnilar bilan gurunglashishni **yaxshi ko'radi**.

sentences.text: Why do you **hate flying**? — I get nervous during take-off.
sentences.translation: Nega **samolyotda uchishni yomon ko'rasiz**? — Uchish paytida asabiylashaman.

sentences.text: Kate **can't bear seeing** animals in small cages at the zoo.
sentences.translation: Keyt hayvonot bog'idagi kichkina qafaslarda hayvonlarni **ko'rishga chiday olmaydi**.

sentences.text: Bekzod doesn't **like being** interrupted when he's working on something important.
sentences.translation: Bekzod muhim ish ustida o'tirganda **gapini bo'lishlarini yoqtirmaydi**.

sentences.text: Children usually **love playing** in the snow, but they hate getting cold.
sentences.translation: Bolalar odatda **qorda o'ynashni yaxshi ko'radi**, lekin sovqotishni yomon ko'radi.

examples.title: **like to do**: habits and good ideas
examples.description: like to do — zavq emas, biror ishni to'g'ri yoki foydali deb bilib, odat qilish. O'zbekchada «-ishni odat qilgan», «-ishni ma'qul ko'radi».

sentences.text: I **like to get** to the airport at least two hours early, just in case.
sentences.translation: Har ehtimolga qarshi aeroportga kamida ikki soat oldin **yetib borishni ma'qul ko'raman**.

sentences.text: Emma **likes to check** her emails before breakfast, so the day starts calmly.
sentences.translation: Kun xotirjam boshlanishi uchun Emma nonushtadan oldin pochtasini **tekshirib olishni odat qilgan**.

sentences.text: We **like to pay** our bills as soon as they arrive.
sentences.translation: Hisoblar kelishi bilan ularni **to'lab qo'yishni ma'qul ko'ramiz**.

sentences.text: My father **likes to have** his car serviced every six months.
sentences.translation: Dadam mashinasini har olti oyda **texnik ko'rikdan o'tkazib turishni odat qilgan**.

sentences.text: Dilnoza **likes to plan** every detail of a trip before she books anything.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza biror narsani bron qilishdan oldin sayohatning har bir tafsilotini **rejalashtirib olishni yaxshi ko'radi**.

sentences.text: Before an important meeting, I **like to read** through my notes one more time.
sentences.translation: Muhim yig'ilish oldidan qaydlarimni yana bir marta **o'qib chiqishni odat qilganman**.

sentences.text: Jasur **likes to keep** some cash in his wallet in case the card machine doesn't work.
sentences.translation: Karta terminali ishlamay qolsa, deb Jasur hamyonida biroz naqd pul **olib yurishni ma'qul ko'radi**.

sentences.text: Our teacher **likes to start** each lesson with a short quiz.
sentences.translation: O'qituvchimiz har bir darsni qisqa test bilan **boshlashni odat qilgan**.

sentences.text: I don't **like to disturb** people after nine in the evening, so I'll call tomorrow.
sentences.translation: Kechqurun soat to'qqizdan keyin odamlarni **bezovta qilishni xush ko'rmayman**, ertaga qo'ng'iroq qilaman.

sentences.text: How often do you **like to back up** your work? — Every Friday, without fail.
sentences.translation: Ishingizning zaxira nusxasini qanchalik tez-tez **olib turishni ma'qul ko'rasiz**? — Har juma, kanda qilmay.

examples.title: Contrast: **like doing** or **like to do**?
examples.description: Juft gaplar: birinchisi — zavq (like / love doing), ikkinchisi — odat yoki to'g'ri deb bilish (like to do).

sentences.text: I **like swimming** — it's my favourite way to relax after work.
sentences.translation: **Suzish menga yoqadi** — ishdan keyin dam olishning eng sevimli usulim.

sentences.text: I **like to swim** three times a week because it's good for my back.
sentences.translation: Belimga foydali bo'lgani uchun haftada uch marta **suzishni odat qilganman**.

sentences.text: Madina **loves cooking**, especially for big family dinners.
sentences.translation: Madina **ovqat pishirishni juda yaxshi ko'radi**, ayniqsa katta oilaviy dasturxonlarga.

sentences.text: Madina **likes to cook** at home rather than eat out, because it's cheaper.
sentences.translation: Arzonroq bo'lgani uchun Madina tashqarida ovqatlangandan ko'ra uyda **ovqat qilishni ma'qul ko'radi**.

sentences.text: James **doesn't like cleaning** the bathroom — nobody does!
sentences.translation: Jeymsga **hammom tozalash yoqmaydi** — hech kimga yoqmaydi!

sentences.text: Still, he **likes to clean** it every Saturday so that it never gets too dirty.
sentences.translation: Shunday bo'lsa ham, haddan tashqari kirlanib ketmasligi uchun uni har shanba **tozalab turishni ma'qul ko'radi**.

sentences.text: Do you **like getting up** early? — Not at all, but I have to.
sentences.translation: Erta **turishni yaxshi ko'rasizmi**? — Umuman yo'q, lekin majburman.

sentences.text: Aziz **likes to get up** early on exam days to revise one last time.
sentences.translation: Imtihon kunlari Aziz oxirgi marta takrorlab olish uchun **erta turishni ma'qul ko'radi**.

sentences.text: Sarah **hates driving** in the city, but she **likes to drive** her kids to school herself.
sentences.translation: Sara shaharda **mashina haydashni yomon ko'radi**, lekin bolalarini maktabga o'zi **olib borishni ma'qul ko'radi**.

sentences.text: Tom **loves eating** chocolate, but he **likes to limit** himself to one bar a week.
sentences.translation: Tom **shokolad yeyishni juda yaxshi ko'radi**, lekin o'zini haftasiga bitta plitka bilan **cheklashni to'g'ri deb biladi**.

examples.title: **enjoy**, **mind**, **can't stand**; **I hate to** say ...
examples.description: enjoy, mind, dislike, can't stand — faqat -ing. can't bear — ikkalasi. I hate to interrupt / say — kechirim so'rab boshlanadigan gap.

sentences.text: Do you **enjoy working** night shifts, or do you just need the money?
sentences.translation: Tungi smenada **ishlash sizga yoqadimi** yoki shunchaki pul kerakmi?

sentences.text: I **hate to interrupt**, but your taxi is waiting outside.
sentences.translation: **Gapingizni bo'lganim uchun uzr**, lekin taksingiz tashqarida kutyapti.

sentences.text: My brother **dislikes talking** about his feelings, even with his wife.
sentences.translation: Akam hatto xotini bilan ham his-tuyg'ulari haqida **gaplashishni yoqtirmaydi**.

sentences.text: I **hate to say** this, but I don't think your plan will work.
sentences.translation: **Aytishga tilim bormaydi-yu**, lekin menimcha rejangiz ish bermaydi.

sentences.text: Would you **mind waiting** here while I find the manager?
sentences.translation: Men menejerni topib kelgunimcha shu yerda **kutib turmaysizmi**?

sentences.text: Kate **doesn't mind sharing** an office as long as it's quiet.
sentences.translation: Tinch bo'lsa, Keyt kabinetni boshqalar bilan **bo'lishishga qarshi emas**.

sentences.text: Sarah **can't stand being** late, so she always leaves home far too early.
sentences.translation: Sara **kechikishga toqat qila olmaydi**, shuning uchun uydan doim juda erta chiqadi.

sentences.text: Our neighbours **hate seeing** litter in the street, so they pick it up themselves.
sentences.translation: Qo'shnilarimiz ko'chada axlat **ko'rishni yomon ko'radi**, shuning uchun o'zlari terib olishadi.

sentences.text: Most students **enjoy taking** part in debates once they lose their fear of speaking.
sentences.translation: Gapirishdan qo'rqmay qo'yishgach, ko'pchilik talabalar munozaralarda **qatnashishni yoqtirib qoladi**.

sentences.text: Jasur **can't bear to throw** anything away — his garage is full of old things.
sentences.translation: Jasur hech narsani **tashlab yuborishga ko'zi qiymaydi** — garaji eski narsalarga to'la.

examples.title: **would like / love / hate / prefer** + **to**
examples.description: would bilan — aniq vaziyatdagi istak, taklif yoki xohlamaslik; deyarli doim **to**. O'zbekchada «-moqchiman», «istardim», «sira istamasdim».

sentences.text: I'd **like to book** a table for four at eight o'clock, please.
sentences.translation: Soat sakkizga to'rt kishilik stol **band qilmoqchi edim**.

sentences.text: Would you **like to join** us for dinner on Friday? — I'd **love to**!
sentences.translation: Juma kuni biz bilan kechki ovqatga **qo'shilasizmi**? — **Jon deb**!

sentences.text: Dilnoza **would love to study** in Edinburgh, but the fees are very high.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza Edinburgda **o'qishni juda istardi**, lekin o'qish to'lovi juda baland.

sentences.text: I'd **hate to live** in a big city — it's far too noisy for me.
sentences.translation: Katta shaharda **yashashni sira istamasdim** — men uchun haddan tashqari shovqinli.

sentences.text: Would you **prefer to meet** at the office or somewhere more relaxed?
sentences.translation: Ofisda **uchrashishni afzal ko'rasizmi** yoki qulayroq joydami?

sentences.text: Tom **would like** his parents **to visit** him in London next summer.
sentences.translation: Tom kelasi yoz ota-onasining Londonga **mehmonga kelishini istaydi**.

sentences.text: What **would** you **like to do** when you retire? — Travel, definitely.
sentences.translation: Nafaqaga chiqqach, nima **qilishni istaysiz**? — Albatta, sayohat.

sentences.text: We'd **love to come** to your wedding, but we'll be in Samarkand that weekend.
sentences.translation: To'yingizga **kelishni juda istardik**, lekin o'sha dam olish kunlari Samarqandda bo'lamiz.

sentences.text: I wouldn't **like to be** in his shoes when the boss finds out.
sentences.translation: Boshliq bilib qolganda, **uning o'rnida bo'lishni istamasdim**.

sentences.text: Oliver **would hate to miss** the final, so he's booked a day off work.
sentences.translation: Oliver finalni **o'tkazib yuborishni sira istamaydi**, shuning uchun ishdan bir kunlik ruxsat olgan.

examples.title: **Do you like ...?** or **Would you like ...?**
examples.description: Juft gaplar: like -ing — umuman yaxshi ko'rish (did), would like to — aniq vaziyatdagi istak yoki taklif.

sentences.text: Do you **like dancing**? — Yes, but only at weddings!
sentences.translation: **Raqs tushishni yaxshi ko'rasizmi**? — Ha, lekin faqat to'ylarda!

sentences.text: Would you **like to dance**? — Thank you, but my feet are killing me.
sentences.translation: **Raqsga tushasizmi**? — Rahmat, lekin oyoqlarim juda og'riyapti.

sentences.text: I **like visiting** my grandparents in the village — it's so peaceful there.
sentences.translation: Qishloqdagi bobo-buvimnikiga **borishni yaxshi ko'raman** — u yer juda osoyishta.

sentences.text: I'd **like to visit** them this weekend, if the weather is good.
sentences.translation: Ob-havo yaxshi bo'lsa, bu dam olish kunlari ularnikiga **borib kelmoqchiman**.

sentences.text: Does Aziz **like playing** football? — He loves it; he plays every Sunday.
sentences.translation: Aziz **futbol o'ynashni yaxshi ko'radimi**? — Juda; har yakshanba o'ynaydi.

sentences.text: Would Aziz **like to play** for our team in the tournament?
sentences.translation: Aziz musobaqada bizning jamoa uchun **o'ynashni xohlarmikan**?

sentences.text: Emma **loves travelling** by train because she can read on the way.
sentences.translation: Yo'lda kitob o'qiy olgani uchun Emma **poyezdda sayohat qilishni juda yaxshi ko'radi**.

sentences.text: Emma **would love to travel** across Europe by train one day.
sentences.translation: Emma qachondir Yevropa bo'ylab poyezdda **sayohat qilishni juda istardi**.

sentences.text: My parents **don't like eating** out — they think restaurants are too expensive.
sentences.translation: Ota-onam **tashqarida ovqatlanishni yoqtirmaydi** — ular restoranlarni juda qimmat deb hisoblashadi.

sentences.text: Would your parents **like to come** with us to the new Uzbek restaurant tonight?
sentences.translation: Ota-onang bugun kechqurun biz bilan yangi o'zbek restoraniga **borishni xohlasharmikan**?

examples.title: **would like to have done**: missed chances
examples.description: Amalga oshmagan o'tgan istak: would like to have done = would have liked to do. would love / hate / prefer bilan ham shunday.

sentences.text: I'd **like to have seen** the exhibition, but it closed before I got back from Oxford.
sentences.translation: Ko'rgazmani **ko'rishni istagan edim**, lekin men Oksforddan qaytgunimcha yopilib qoldi.

sentences.text: We **would have liked to stay** longer in Khiva, but our train left at six.
sentences.translation: Xivada uzoqroq **qolishni istagan edik**, lekin poyezdimiz soat oltida jo'nab ketdi.

sentences.text: Kate **would love to have been** at her sister's graduation, but she was ill.
sentences.translation: Keyt singlisining bitiruv marosimida **bo'lishni juda istagan edi**, lekin kasal edi.

sentences.text: My grandfather **would like to have studied** medicine, but the war changed his plans.
sentences.translation: Bobom **tibbiyot o'qishni istagan edi**, lekin urush uning rejalarini o'zgartirib yubordi.

sentences.text: I **would hate to have missed** your wedding — thank you for changing the date!
sentences.translation: To'yingizni **o'tkazib yuborsam, juda achinardim** — sanani o'zgartirganingiz uchun rahmat!

sentences.text: Jasur **would have liked to say** goodbye to everyone, but he had to leave in a hurry.
sentences.translation: Jasur hamma bilan **xayrlashishni istagan edi**, lekin shoshilib ketishiga to'g'ri keldi.

sentences.text: Sarah **would like to have met** your parents — maybe next time.
sentences.translation: Sara ota-onangiz bilan **tanishishni istagan edi** — balki keyingi safar.

sentences.text: Did you see the eclipse? — No, I'd **love to have seen** it, but it was cloudy.
sentences.translation: Tutilishni ko'rdingizmi? — Yo'q, **juda ko'rishni istagan edim**, lekin havo bulutli edi.

sentences.text: The company **would have preferred to hire** someone with more experience.
sentences.translation: Kompaniya ko'proq tajribaga ega odamni **ishga olishni afzal ko'rgan bo'lardi**.

sentences.text: Looking back, Nilufar **would like to have spent** more time with her grandmother.
sentences.translation: Ortga nazar tashlab, Nilufar buvisi bilan ko'proq vaqt **o'tkazgan bo'lishni istaydi**.

examples.title: Dialogue: planning a weekend away
examples.description: Aralash mustahkamlash: dam olish kunlarini rejalashtirayotgan ikki do'st — would like to, love -ing, like to, hate, can't stand, would like to have done.

sentences.text: — Would you **like to go** away somewhere next weekend? We both need a break.
sentences.translation: — Kelasi dam olish kunlari biror joyga **borib kelishni xohlaysanmi**? Ikkalamizga ham dam kerak.

sentences.text: — I'd **love to**! But you know I **hate spending** hours in the car.
sentences.translation: — **Jon deb**! Lekin bilasan-ku, mashinada soatlab **o'tirishni yomon ko'raman**.

sentences.text: — Then how about the train to Samarkand? I **like to book** early to get cheap seats.
sentences.translation: — Unda Samarqandga poyezdda-chi? Arzon joy olish uchun **oldindan bron qilishni odat qilganman**.

sentences.text: — Perfect. I **love walking** around the old city in the evening.
sentences.translation: — Zo'r. Kechqurun eski shahar bo'ylab **sayr qilishni juda yaxshi ko'raman**.

sentences.text: — Me too. Last time I'd **like to have seen** the observatory, but it was closed.
sentences.translation: — Men ham. O'tgan safar rasadxonani **ko'rishni istagan edim**, lekin yopiq edi.

sentences.text: — Then let's go there first. Do you **enjoy visiting** museums as well?
sentences.translation: — Unda avval o'sha yerga boramiz. Muzeylarni **aylanish ham senga yoqadimi**?

sentences.text: — Not really. I **can't stand reading** every little sign — I just like looking around.
sentences.translation: — Unchalik emas. Har bir kichik yozuvni **o'qishga toqatim yo'q** — shunchaki atrofni tomosha qilishni yoqtiraman.

sentences.text: — Fair enough. Would your sister **like to come** with us too?
sentences.translation: — Mayli. Opang ham biz bilan **borishni xohlarmikan**?

sentences.text: — She'd **hate to miss** a trip like that, so I'll ask her tonight.
sentences.translation: — U bunday sayohatni **o'tkazib yuborishni sira istamaydi**, bugun kechqurun so'rayman.

sentences.text: — Great. I don't **like to leave** things until the last minute, so let's book now.
sentences.translation: — Ajoyib. Ishlarni oxirgi daqiqaga **qoldirishni yoqtirmayman**, keling, hozir bron qilamiz.
